_note: Approximate demo data so the app runs before the real database is loaded. Figures are indicative annual costs in EUR for international students and should be replaced via `python manage.py import_universities`.

universities.name: Delft University of Technology
universities.scholarship_notes: Justus & Louise van Effen scholarship covers tuition plus €16,000 for outstanding non-EU applicants.
universities.description: The Netherlands' oldest technical university, strongest in aerospace, civil and industrial design.

universities.name: University of Amsterdam
universities.scholarship_notes: Amsterdam Merit Scholarship: €5,000–€25,000 for non-EEA students.
universities.description: A large research university spread through the city centre, with a wide English-taught bachelor catalogue.

universities.name: Erasmus University Rotterdam
universities.scholarship_notes: Erasmus Trustfonds scholarships and the Holland Scholarship (€5,000, first year).
universities.description: Business and economics powerhouse, with the Rotterdam School of Management at its centre.

universities.name: Eindhoven University of Technology
universities.scholarship_notes: TU/e Bachelor Scholarship covers part of tuition for non-EEA students.
universities.description: Engineering-only campus embedded in the Brainport tech region, very close to industry.

universities.name: University of Groningen
universities.scholarship_notes: Holland Scholarship €5,000 and the Groningen Talent Grant.
universities.description: A classic Dutch university town where students are a third of the population.

universities.name: Maastricht University
universities.scholarship_notes: UM Holland-High Potential Scholarship covers tuition, insurance and living costs.
universities.description: Problem-based learning in small groups; the most internationally mixed campus in the country.

universities.name: Technical University of Munich
universities.scholarship_notes: Deutschlandstipendium €300/month; no tuition beyond the semester fee.
universities.description: Germany's top-ranked technical university. Semester fee only, but Munich is expensive to live in.

universities.name: Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich
universities.scholarship_notes: Deutschlandstipendium and DAAD scholarships for international students.
universities.description: One of Europe's oldest universities; most bachelor teaching is in German, masters often in English.

universities.name: Heidelberg University
universities.scholarship_notes: Baden-Württemberg charges €1,500/semester for non-EU students; DAAD grants can offset it.
universities.description: Germany's oldest university, with real strength in medicine and the life sciences.

universities.name: RWTH Aachen University
universities.scholarship_notes: No tuition; Deutschlandstipendium available on merit.
universities.description: The largest engineering faculty in Germany, with deep ties to the automotive industry.

universities.name: Technical University of Berlin
universities.scholarship_notes: No tuition fees; Berlin has a well-developed student housing network.
universities.description: Technical university in the middle of Berlin, strong in computing and urban systems.

universities.name: Sorbonne University
universities.scholarship_notes: Non-EU differentiated fees can be waived; Eiffel Excellence Scholarship for top applicants.
universities.description: Humanities and sciences across the Latin Quarter, with partial exemptions common for non-EU students.

universities.name: Sciences Po
universities.scholarship_notes: Needs-based tuition: fees scale with family income, and can reach zero.
universities.description: France's school for politics and public affairs. Income-scaled fees make it cheaper than the sticker price.

universities.name: École Polytechnique
universities.scholarship_notes: Bachelor scholarships cover 60–100% of tuition for high-scoring applicants.
universities.description: Highly selective grande école with a mathematics-first bachelor taught entirely in English.

universities.name: Grenoble Alpes University
universities.scholarship_notes: IDEX scholarships of €5,000–€10,000 per year for international bachelor students.
universities.description: Research campus in the Alps, strong in physics, computing and environmental science.

universities.name: Bocconi University
universities.scholarship_notes: Merit awards fully waive tuition for the top of the applicant pool; need-based aid is income-tested.
universities.description: Italy's leading business and economics school, with a strong graduate placement record.

universities.name: Politecnico di Milano
universities.scholarship_notes: Income-based fee bands mean many international students pay well under the maximum.
universities.description: Top-ranked in design and architecture in Europe, and strong across engineering.

universities.name: University of Bologna
universities.scholarship_notes: Unibo Action 1 & 2 study grants: €11,000 plus tuition waiver.
universities.description: The oldest university in continuous operation, with a growing set of English-taught degrees.

universities.name: Sapienza University of Rome
universities.scholarship_notes: Fees are ISEE income-banded; low-income international students can pay the minimum.
universities.description: One of Europe's largest universities by enrolment, in the centre of Rome.

universities.name: Politecnico di Torino
universities.scholarship_notes: TOPoliTO merit scholarships waive fees and add a €6,000 stipend.
universities.description: Engineering school with a long-standing automotive specialism and English-taught tracks.

universities.name: IE University
universities.scholarship_notes: Merit scholarships of 15–100% of tuition, assessed at application.
universities.description: Private, entirely English-taught, with the highest fees on this list but generous merit aid.

universities.name: University of Barcelona
universities.scholarship_notes: Fee reductions for high-performing students; regional grants for non-EU applicants are limited.
universities.description: Spain's highest-ranked public university, mostly teaching in Catalan and Spanish at bachelor level.

universities.name: Carlos III University of Madrid
universities.scholarship_notes: Excellence scholarships covering 50–100% of tuition for strong entry grades.
universities.description: Public university with a large English-taught bilingual programme, strong in economics and engineering.

universities.name: Trinity College Dublin
universities.scholarship_notes: Global Excellence Scholarships of €5,000–€10,000 per year.
universities.description: Ireland's oldest university, in the middle of Dublin, entirely English-taught.

universities.name: University College Dublin
universities.scholarship_notes: UCD Global Excellence Scholarship: up to 100% of tuition for exceptional applicants.
universities.description: Large parkland campus outside the city centre, with a broad international intake.

universities.name: University of Warsaw
universities.scholarship_notes: Tuition waivers for high-achieving international students; living costs are among Europe's lowest.
universities.description: Poland's leading university, with English-taught tracks in economics, IR and computing.

universities.name: AGH University of Science and Technology
universities.scholarship_notes: Low flat fees for non-EU students; no separate application fee.
universities.description: Technical university in Kraków with English-taught engineering and computing degrees.

universities.name: Jagiellonian University
universities.scholarship_notes: Partial fee waivers for students with strong secondary results.
universities.description: Founded in 1364; the English-taught medical programme draws students from across Europe.

universities.name: Charles University
universities.scholarship_notes: Czech-taught programmes are free of tuition for everyone, including international students.
universities.description: Study in Czech and pay nothing; study in English and pay a moderate fee.

universities.name: Czech Technical University in Prague
universities.scholarship_notes: No tuition for Czech-taught study; English programmes charge a flat annual fee.
universities.description: Engineering and architecture, with a well-regarded computer science faculty.

universities.name: Budapest University of Technology and Economics
universities.scholarship_notes: Stipendium Hungaricum covers tuition, accommodation and a monthly allowance.
universities.description: Hungary's main technical university, with a long-running English-taught engineering track.

universities.name: Eötvös Loránd University
universities.scholarship_notes: Stipendium Hungaricum and partial tuition waivers.
universities.description: Broad research university with English-taught programmes in science and social science.

universities.name: University of Porto
universities.scholarship_notes: Merit scholarships for international students; Porto is cheap to live in by western European standards.
universities.description: Portugal's largest university, with a strong engineering faculty and low living costs.

universities.name: University of Lisbon
universities.scholarship_notes: Instituto Superior Técnico offers merit awards for international entrants.
universities.description: Includes Instituto Superior Técnico, the country's leading engineering school.

universities.name: NOVA University Lisbon
universities.scholarship_notes: NOVA SBE merit scholarships for economics and management applicants.
universities.description: Modern campus with English-taught economics and management on a seafront site.

universities.name: TU Wien
universities.scholarship_notes: Non-EU tuition is €726.72 per semester — among the lowest in western Europe.
universities.description: Technical university in central Vienna; very low fees for a high-income city.

universities.name: University of Vienna
universities.scholarship_notes: Low flat fees plus performance grants for international students.
universities.description: Austria's largest university, with bachelor teaching mainly in German.

universities.name: ETH Zurich
universities.scholarship_notes: Tuition is nominal; the Excellence Scholarship covers living costs for top applicants.
universities.description: Europe's strongest technical university. Fees are tiny, but Zurich living costs are the highest here.

universities.name: EPFL
universities.scholarship_notes: Excellence Fellowships for masters; bachelor fees are low but living costs are not.
universities.description: Lakeside campus with a dominant computer science and robotics faculty.

universities.name: KTH Royal Institute of Technology
universities.scholarship_notes: KTH Scholarship covers full tuition for non-EU students; the Swedish Institute funds living costs.
universities.description: Sweden's largest technical university, entirely English-taught at masters level.

universities.name: Lund University
universities.scholarship_notes: Lund Global Scholarship covers 25–100% of tuition.
universities.description: A traditional university town twenty minutes from Copenhagen.

universities.name: Uppsala University
universities.scholarship_notes: Uppsala University Global Scholarship covers tuition in full for a small number of students.
universities.description: Scandinavia's oldest university, with strong life sciences.

universities.name: Technical University of Denmark
universities.scholarship_notes: Danish Government Scholarships cover tuition plus a living stipend for a few non-EU students.
universities.description: Engineering-only campus north of Copenhagen, with heavy industry collaboration.

universities.name: University of Copenhagen
universities.scholarship_notes: Free for EU/EEA students; non-EU pay tuition with limited scholarship places.
universities.description: Denmark's flagship university, especially strong in health and natural sciences.

universities.name: Aalto University
universities.scholarship_notes: Aalto scholarships waive 50–100% of tuition for non-EU students.
universities.description: Technology, business and design merged into one campus — unusual and well executed.

universities.name: University of Helsinki
universities.scholarship_notes: Finland Scholarship covers first-year tuition plus a €5,000 relocation grant.
universities.description: Broad research university; most bachelor teaching is in Finnish or Swedish.

universities.name: Norwegian University of Science and Technology
universities.scholarship_notes: Norway introduced tuition for non-EEA students in 2023; Quota Scheme places are limited.
universities.description: Norway's engineering university, with a strong marine and energy focus.

universities.name: University of Oslo
universities.scholarship_notes: Non-EEA tuition applies; some faculties offer partial waivers.
universities.description: Norway's oldest university, with English-taught masters across the sciences.

universities.name: KU Leuven
universities.scholarship_notes: Science@Leuven scholarships for non-EEA students, partly covering fees and living costs.
universities.description: Belgium's leading research university, in a compact student town near Brussels.

universities.name: Ghent University
universities.scholarship_notes: Top-up grants for students from developing countries; fees are flat and low.
universities.description: Strong in bioscience and veterinary medicine, with growing English-taught provision.

universities.name: University of Tartu
universities.scholarship_notes: Tuition waivers plus a €400/month stipend for the strongest applicants.
universities.description: The Baltics' leading university, with English-taught computer science and a low cost of living.

universities.name: Tallinn University of Technology
universities.scholarship_notes: Performance-based tuition waivers reviewed each semester.
universities.description: Estonia's technical university, known for cybersecurity and digital government programmes.

universities.name: Riga Technical University
universities.scholarship_notes: Low flat fees; state scholarships available after the first year.
universities.description: Latvia's engineering university, with English-taught bachelor programmes and low fees.

universities.name: Vilnius University
universities.scholarship_notes: State scholarships for international students; fees are among the lowest in the EU.
universities.description: The oldest university in the Baltics, with a growing English-taught catalogue.

universities.name: University of Bucharest
universities.scholarship_notes: Romanian government scholarships cover tuition and accommodation for selected applicants.
universities.description: Romania's largest university; very low fees and living costs.

universities.name: Babeș-Bolyai University
universities.scholarship_notes: Fee exemptions for students with strong baccalaureate results.
universities.description: Multilingual university in Transylvania, with English and Hungarian-taught tracks.

universities.name: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens
universities.scholarship_notes: English-taught programmes charge tuition; Greek-taught study is free.
universities.description: Greece's oldest university, with a handful of English-taught degrees.

universities.name: University of Manchester
universities.scholarship_notes: Global Futures Scholarship: £5,000 per year for international undergraduates.
universities.description: A large civic university with one of the UK's biggest international intakes.

universities.name: University of Edinburgh
universities.scholarship_notes: Edinburgh Global Undergraduate Scholarship: £5,000 per year, needs-assessed.
universities.description: Historic campus woven through the old town, strong in informatics and medicine.

universities.name: University of Warwick
universities.scholarship_notes: Warwick Undergraduate Global Excellence Scholarship covers part of tuition.
universities.description: Self-contained campus university with a dominant economics and mathematics reputation.

universities.name: University of Glasgow
universities.scholarship_notes: Undergraduate Excellence Scholarship of £5,000 per year for international students.
universities.description: One of the UK's oldest universities, on a gothic campus in the west end of the city.
